toyota_summary:
The Irish EU presidency proposed a compromise emissions package today that would tighten the 2035 carbon reduction target for vehicles. The specifics remain unclear from available reporting, but the move signals that EU member states want stricter rules than currently negotiated, pushing the bloc toward harder climate requirements for automakers selling in Europe.

This matters because Europe is already the world's most demanding emissions market. Tighter 2035 targets would force faster electrification across product lines and accelerate the phase-out of internal combustion engines earlier than many manufacturers planned. Higher compliance costs would ripple across global supply chains, since automakers typically engineer vehicles to meet the strictest market standard and sell them worldwide.

Watch whether Germany and France block or accept the Irish proposal in upcoming Council votes.

emails.subject_en: Irish Council presidency proposes stricter emissions target for automakers
emails.summary_en: Ireland's EU Council presidency has proposed keeping a 90% emissions reduction target for automakers by 2035, compared to 2021 levels, allowing offsets through alternative fuels and low-carbon steel and aluminum investments. This stance is stricter than the European Parliament's 87.5% target and firmer than the France-Germany compromise, though it declines to create a separate vehicle category for alternative-fuel-only cars. The proposal also freezes the utility factor—used to measure plug-in hybrid electric motor usage—until January 2030, aligning with Parliament's position.
emails.summary_ja: アイルランドのEU理事会議長国は、自動車メーカーに対する2035年の排出削減目標を2021年比90%に据え置く妥協案を提示し、代替燃料や低炭素鋼・アルミニウムへの投資による相殺を認める方針だ。この立場は欧州議会の87.5%目標より厳しく、仏独の妥協案よりも強硬だが、代替燃料専用車の新カテゴリー創設は見送る。また、プラグインハイブリッド車の電気モーター使用率を示す「ユーティリティファクター」を2030年1月まで凍結する案も盛り込まれ、これは欧州議会委員会の立場と一致している。
